items.prompt:
Which list is correct?
A) pens paper and glue
B) pens, paper, and glue
C) pens paper, and glue

Which correctly sets off the introductory element?
A) After the storm the sun came out.
B) After the storm, the sun came out.
C) After, the storm the sun came out.
items.answer: B) After the storm, the sun came out.

steps: Comma after intro. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) After the storm, the sun came out.

items.prompt:
Which correctly uses a comma in direct address?
A) Can you help me Tom?
B) Can you help me, Tom?
C) Can you, help me Tom?
items.answer: B) Can you help me, Tom?

steps: Set off the name. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) Can you help me, Tom?

items.prompt:
Which correctly sets off 'however'?
A) However she was late.
B) However, she was late.
C) However she, was late.

steps: Comma after intro word. Key is B.

items.prompt:
How should the title of a BOOK be shown?
A) in quotation marks
B) in italics or underlined
C) in all capitals only

steps: Long works = italics. Key is B.

items.prompt:
A SHORT poem's title should be in:
A) italics
B) quotation marks
C) nothing

steps: Short works = quotes. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
A) Yes I agree and I will help.
B) Yes, I agree, and I will help.
C) Yes I agree, and I will help
items.answer: B) Yes, I agree, and I will help.

steps: Set off 'Yes'; comma before 'and' joining clauses. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) Yes, I agree, and I will help.

items.prompt:
Which correctly sets off the extra (nonrestrictive) clause?
A) My dog which is small barks a lot.
B) My dog, which is small, barks a lot.
C) My dog which is small, barks a lot.
items.answer: B) My dog, which is small, barks a lot.

steps: Commas around the clause. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) My dog, which is small, barks a lot.
